title: Membrane excitability and synaptic transmission
source_evidence: Full official L56–57 publisher captions through closing activities and all29 assigned topics; bounded visual audit of8 contact sheets,133 sampled stills,15 native reopens. No continuous video/audio.

coverage_topics.disposition: Define membrane voltage as inside minus outside, with compartment/site and no-signaling assumption; −70 mV is an illustrative neuron, not every cell or compartment.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep pump/leak mechanisms, reject literal universal time sequence 0→−5→−90→−70 mV. The slide itself labels a starting −70 mV while captions call 0 mV hypothetical.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep ATPase stoichiometry 3 Na out/2 K in per cycle and electrogenic current; −5 mV is not a fixed voltage made by one pump cycle. Distinguish direct pump current from long-term gradient maintenance; osmotic water follows total osmolarity, not a slogan that Na alone bursts cells.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep K-selective resting conductance and outward K driving force for a specified resting state; −90 mV is an approximate K equilibrium example, not an automatic second stage. Do not call Cl universally impermeant/fixed merely because some intracellular anions are impermeant.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep Na leak inward under a typical gradient. Mixed-ion conductance and active restoration determine steady rest; channel number alone is not conductance and Na entry does not invariably contribute an exact +20 mV.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep a **single-ion** electrochemical equilibrium/reversal-potential construction; zero net flux of that permeant ion at equilibrium does not mean all ions cease moving or pumps stop at physiological rest.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Native slide visibly gives `E_X=(RT/zF) ln([X]out/[X]in)`; specify V_inside−V_outside, signed valence, positive activities or ideal dilute concentration approximation, absolute Kelvin T, and volts-to-mV conversion. For K, out/in<1 gives negative E_K; for Na, out/in>1 gives positive E_Na.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Graded response amplitude/location/time depend on stimulus and conductance; passive spread decays, unlike regenerated axonal AP. Slide-only text explicitly names local amplitude and receptor binding.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Ligand-gated channels are one common postsynaptic route; mechanically gated and other graded inputs also exist. Presynaptic release precedes postsynaptic channel action; do not conflate a channel and the transmitter.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Define EPSP/IPSP by effect on spike likelihood in stated state, not fixed −55/−90 mV endpoints or by transmitter name alone. Slide calls balance important.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Keep a concrete excitatory ligand-gated conductance example, with receptor identity and reversal potential; Na/Ca influx depends on channel permeability and driving force, so no universal one-EPSP-to-threshold jump.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: GABA can activate GABA-A anion conductance or GABA-B G-protein pathways; inhibition may be hyperpolarizing or shunting, sometimes depolarizing without excitation. Do not force every inhibitory response to Cl influx, K efflux or −90 mV.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Integrate excitatory and inhibitory conductances at a specified trigger region with decay and membrane state; not simple addition of universal voltage increments.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Retain temporal and spatial summation with differing time constants, dendritic location and sign; native 30:30 shows repeated inputs before decay and threshold illustration. Do not claim simultaneous distinct sources must make a faster AP.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Answer the pump-stop closing activity in two timescales: immediate loss of electrogenic pump current versus subsequent Na/K-gradient dissipation and voltage change under continued conductances. Neither instant −5 mV subtraction nor instant 0 mV is general. Native 32:00 plasticity slide is a qualitative aside, not a quantified practice-to-memory law.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: AP is a locally regenerative membrane-voltage event with threshold in specified cell/state; all-or-none amplitude is not fixed across all axons/conditions. Native 03:00 banner explicitly says slide/caption use of **IPSP for EPSP is mistaken**.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Fast inward Na current can drive axonal upstroke under typical gradients; −55 and +30 mV are schematic values, not exact activation/peak switches.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Separate voltage-gated Na activation and availability/inactivation. Do not make channels fully open only at one voltage, or treat the inactivation gate as slowly opening after activation.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Local axial current depolarizes adjacent membrane; a propagating front has spatially different upstroke/recovery regions. Distinguish within-membrane conduction from transfer across a chemical synapse.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Terminal depolarization opens voltage-gated Ca channels and Ca enters from extracellular fluid under typical conditions; caption 15:19 says Ca “comes outside,” contradicted by its own earlier influx description and native synapse slide.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Delayed K conductance contributes to repolarization; its kinetics overlap Na inactivation, not a switch triggered exactly at +30 mV. Native 12:00 slide itself calls K channels slower.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Na inactivation develops with voltage and time; K activation has its own delay. The available Na inactivation gate is already permissive at rest; subsequent recovery requires repolarization.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Afterhyperpolarization can occur while K conductance persists; −90 mV is not a mandatory endpoint or identical to every K reversal potential.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Ca entry triggers a primed fusion apparatus via Ca-sensing proteins including synaptotagmin; Ca does not simply become a physical bridge between vesicle and membrane SNAREs. Separate docking/priming, fusion pore and transmitter release.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Rebuild voltage-versus-time trace with explicit ms/mV axes, resting/threshold labels as illustrative, locally sequential upstroke/repolarization/afterhyperpolarization; native 23:00 curve has these labels.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Two-gate Na cartoon is a pedagogical channel-state idealization. Rest: activation closed/inactivation available; depolarization activates then inactivates; repolarization recovers availability. Native 26:00 annotated gate scheme and captions wrongly say inactivation opens slowly after activation.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Absolute refractoriness begins during the spike while enough Na channels are unavailable, not only at peak or a fixed one-third waveform. Relative refractoriness depends on partial Na recovery and persistent K conductance/state; “extra EPSP” may work, IPSP is not excitatory stimulation.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Native synaptic slide names vesicle synaptobrevin/v-SNARE, plasma-membrane syntaxin and SNAP-25/t-SNARE; retain locations but distinguish SNARE assembly from Ca sensing by synaptotagmin. Do not imply transmitter clearance occurs automatically at fusion.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending

coverage_topics.disposition: Answer closing channel-perturbation activity with a specified channel, tissue/preparation and causal path. Example: blocked axonal Na channels impair AP propagation, reducing terminal depolarization/Ca entry and release; a terminal Ca-channel perturbation can impair release despite an arriving AP. Avoid drug dosing or individual prediction. Native 32:30 slide adds APs in some muscle/endocrine cells and illustrates frequency 10 versus 100 s⁻¹; these are slide-only illustrative rates, not sourced measurements or universal coding law.
coverage_topics.coverage_status: located in author draft; independent review pending
